subject.title: fix(codex): bound app-server websocket handshake waits at 30s

question: Should Codex WebSocket and Unix app-server handshakes use an unconditional 30-second cap with `exit` as the guaranteed terminal signal, or should the budget and error semantics be aligned with the existing app-server request-timeout contract?
rationale: The patch deliberately changes fail-closed timing and transport observability for existing custom app-server setups; tests establish mechanics but cannot determine the intended compatibility contract.

options.title: Approve the fixed transport contract
options.body: Remove the unrelated CodeQL change, keep the 30-second cap, and lock the `error`/`exit` behavior with focused compatibility tests.

options.title: Align with the existing timeout budget
options.body: Derive the handshake deadline from the existing app-server request-timeout policy so operator-configured budgets remain authoritative.

options.title: Pause the timeout change
options.body: Keep this PR open or close it until an owner chooses the supported custom app-server handshake and terminal-event contract.

recommendation.title: Approve the fixed transport contract
recommendation.body: Remove the unrelated CodeQL change, keep the 30-second cap, and lock the `error`/`exit` behavior with focused compatibility tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The behavior originates in the Codex harness this contributor introduced, and recent history shows continued involvement in Codex app-server decisions.
